policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'So the curse that is causeless alighteth not' renders the negative particle: the verb is negated, which is the ketiv לא (not) with תבא, not the qere ל֣וֹ ('cometh to him'). The hebrew_gloss note 'Hebrew cometh not' makes the negation explicit in the ASV's own report of the Hebrew, leaving no room for the dative reading.

Qere מִדְיָנִים and ketiv מדונים are orthographic variants of the same word for strife/contention; ASV 'a contentious man to inflame strife' renders that sense and cannot distinguish the two spellings. No ASV note is mapped here, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.
ASV 'dissembleth with his lips' is plural, matching the qere בִּשְׂפָתָיו ('with his lips'); the ketiv בשפתו is singular ('with his lip'), which the ASV's plural wording excludes.
